question: Should experimental Claw lifecycle ownership diagnostics become an OpenClaw core Doctor surface after the prerequisite MCP ownership contract lands?
rationale: The code is deliberately gated and bounded, but deciding whether persistent cross-owner lifecycle reconciliation is a supported core capability cannot be inferred from implementation quality or tests alone.

options.title: Defer with the RFC stack
options.body: Keep this PR open but unlanded until maintainers decide the full Claws ownership, reconciliation, and support boundary across the prerequisite and dependent slices.

options.title: Sponsor the core diagnostic
options.body: Accept the experimental core direction, require the gate documentation correction, and land this slice only after its prerequisite ownership contract is accepted.

options.title: Move the direction out of core
options.body: Decline the core lifecycle model if maintainers prefer this capability to remain outside the supported OpenClaw Doctor surface.

recommendation.title: Defer with the RFC stack
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but unlanded until maintainers decide the full Claws ownership, reconciliation, and support boundary across the prerequisite and dependent slices.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and Doctor architecture work makes this person the best available owner for the core-boundary decision.
